name: Zoiper
tagline: A cross-platform SIP softphone for making voice and video calls through your own VoIP provider or PBX.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Zoiper has a free tier plus paid PRO and Biz licenses, historically sold as a one-time per-license purchase rather than a subscription.

verdictSummary: A softphone is a thin shell around a SIP stack, and you are not writing a SIP stack in one session. If your provider or PBX speaks SIP over secure WebSocket, an agent can wire SIP.js into an Electron app and you get registration, inbound and outbound calls, DTMF, hold and call history in a weekend. If your provider only does UDP or TCP SIP, you are suddenly in pjsip or baresip binding territory and the weekend becomes a project. Mobile is the real wall: background wakeups and push for incoming calls mean an iOS or Android build with provider-side push integration, which is exactly the part Zoiper charges for. Codecs beyond Opus and G.711, echo cancellation tuning, and headset button handling are also not something you one-shot.
coreLoopDIY: Registers to your SIP account over WebSocket and places, receives, holds and logs audio calls from a desktop window.
requirements: A SIP account or PBX that accepts SIP over secure WebSocket (WSS)
A STUN server, and a TURN server if you are behind symmetric NAT
Desktop with a working mic and speaker; no mobile build
whatYouLose: Mobile apps with push notifications for incoming calls while the app is closed
Native SIP over UDP and TCP, so providers without WebSocket support are off the table
Licensed codecs like G.729 and iLBC, plus tuned echo cancellation and jitter buffering
Video calls, presence, BLF keys, call transfer and the rest of the PBX feature surface
Years of interop fixes against weird registrars, NAT setups and provider quirks
moatNotes: The moat is not the protocol, which is public and ancient. It is the thousand small compatibility bugs and the mobile push plumbing.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a phone that drops a call or misses an inbound ring is worse than no phone. Zoiper's value is that it has already been pointed at every strange SIP registrar on earth and it works on the phone in your pocket, which is where most people actually need a softphone. A desktop WebRTC build covers the home lab and self-hosted Asterisk crowd fine, but anyone taking real calls for work is paying a one-time fee to never think about jitter buffers again.
notes: Fine if your PBX speaks WSS, otherwise you are writing bindings instead of an app.
prompt:
Build a desktop SIP softphone for personal use. Everything local, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud services.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Electron with TypeScript and Vite, single window.
- SIP.js for signalling and WebRTC for media, SIP over secure WebSocket (WSS) only.
- better-sqlite3 for local call history and contacts, file stored under the app's userData dir.
- Plain CSS, no component library.

Config:
- Read SIP_WS_URI, SIP_URI, SIP_PASSWORD, SIP_DISPLAY_NAME, STUN_URI, optional TURN_URI, TURN_USER, TURN_PASSWORD from a .env file via dotenv in the main process.
- Ship a .env.example. Never log the password.

Features in scope:
- Register to the SIP account on launch, show registration state clearly, auto re-register on failure with backoff.
- Dial pad plus a free text field that accepts a SIP URI or a bare number, outbound audio calls.
- Inbound calls: ring with a local audio file, accept and decline buttons, show caller ID.
- In-call controls: mute, hold, hang up, DTMF via RFC 2833, call timer.
- Audio device pickers for input and output, persisted.
- Call history list in SQLite: direction, remote party, start time, duration, result. Click an entry to redial.
- Contacts: name plus SIP URI, add, edit, delete, searchable, redial from the list.
- A small log panel showing SIP state transitions for debugging, toggleable.

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt:
- SIP over UDP or TCP, native SIP stacks, pjsip or baresip bindings.
- Video calls, presence, BLF, call transfer, conferencing, voicemail MWI.
- Mobile builds, push notifications, background wakeups.
- Licensed codecs; rely on whatever Opus and G.711 the browser engine gives you.

Deliver a README that states plainly that this only works with a provider or PBX exposing SIP over WSS, and tells me how to check that before I waste an evening.
